ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Establishment of Financial Intelligence Unit and the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT Act), Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality, Enforcement Decree of the AML/CFT Act, Financial Services Commission regulations, and the Commercial Act concerning corporate registration and beneficial ownership identification; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) has exclusive government access to beneficial ownership data collected by financial institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Court (Court of Registration, Supreme Court of Korea)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified extract issued by the Commercial Registration Court; notarized by a Korean notary public; then attested by the Apostille Section of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea under the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular legalization is not used because South Korea is an Apostille member state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Court via the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Services (IROS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Official certificate obtained from IROS, notarized, then apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. No consular legalization is required for Apostille member countries.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Company Board of Directors / Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Resolution or PoA executed before a Korean notary, corporate seal certification obtained, then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Apostille destination states only, consular legalization through the Korean consulate in that destination is required instead of the Apostille; the two paths are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and the Korean Commercial Registration Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Articles notarized by a Korean notary public, filed at registration, and then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention destination states. Consular legalization is used solely for non-member states and is an alternative path, not an additional step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Licensed Bank where the preliminary corporate relationship is established or Commercial Bank in the foreign investor country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter signed by an authorized bank officer, bank seal certified, notarized, and then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the competent authority of the country of origin if the bank is located abroad; if the country of origin is not an Apostille member, consular legalization by the destination Korean consulate is the exclusive path.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, and authorized signatory must be screened against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) watchlist, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated lists, and domestic Korean designations under the AML/CFT Act and the Act on Prevention of Financing of Weapons of Mass Destruction. PEPs are risk-rated, including family members and close associates, with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, transaction monitoring, and escalation to KoFIU for suspicious transactions. Screening is continuous, not transaction-only.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS - Internet Registration Services of the Supreme Court of Korea (Commercial Registration and Corporation Registration Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean commercial name must be written in Korean script, with an optional English transliteration, and must contain the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company). The name structure follows a four-tier convention: (1) distinguishing brand or company name; (2) business purpose descriptors where appropriate; (3) legal form suffix; and (4) if used, English name exactly matching the Korean transliteration. Korean statutes require the foreign investor's English name to be phonetically transliterated into Korean when filed, and any inconsistency between Korean and English name spellings may cause registration rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Registration Court rejects a proposed name, the applicant must obtain the written rejection notice, correct the prohibited token, and apply for name re-examination through the same IROS portal. If the applicant believes the rejection is legally erroneous, a formal administrative appeal can be filed with the competent registration court registry under the Commercial Registration Rules within the statutory appeal period. The appeal should attach a legal opinion, the rejected name application receipt, and evidence that the proposed name does not mislead the public or infringe the exclusionary tokens; the court must issue a written decision, and the applicant may escalate through immediate appeal procedures under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act if necessary. Each new name filing requires a fresh registration fee and clearance search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the exclusive registered address for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa if the National Tax Service or a Korean bank determines the entity lacks operational substance. For B2B enterprise SaaS, Korean banks commonly refuse to open corporate accounts with only a virtual office, and the tax office may cancel the business registration if no directors, employees, computers, or business equipment are found at the address. A serviced-office lease with dedicated workspace, signed lease agreement, utility bill, and local management personnel is permissible only if the entity actually conducts management functions there; a pure virtual mailbox without physical presence is high-risk and should be avoided.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk of unannounced inspection by the National Tax Service and local municipal registry officers: Moderate for virtual-office setups, estimated 25-35% probability within the first two years; Low for real leased commercial space, under 10%. Inspection checklist: (1) physical signage or nameplate; (2) lease agreement and rent payment records; (3) employees present and payroll records; (4) IT infrastructure or cloud service documentation; (5) director attendance records and board minutes; (6) bank statements indicating business activity; (7) utility and communication bills; (8) business registration certificate displayed; (9) tax filings demonstrating substance; (10) client contracts and SaaS service apparatus.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), as amended; Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company provisions under Articles 287-2 through 287-73; corporate registration obligation under Article 635; representative director and statutory auditor requirements as set out in the Yuhan Hoesa chapter of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registry Office (Beopwon Deung-gi-so) for the judicial district in which the registered office is located, operated by the National Court Administration; electronic filing accepted through the Supreme Court Internet Registry (Internet Deung-gi-so).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporate Registration accompanied by certified Articles of Incorporation, the practical certificate of paid-in capital deposit, officer consent forms, corporate seal registration, and proof of registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The capital is set in the Articles of Incorporation and must be fully subscribed and paid in before the corporate registration application is filed. The paid-in amount must be deposited into a blocked capital-verification account at a licensed South Korean commercial bank, with the bank issuing a capital verification certificate; funds are released only after corporate registration is completed and a corporate registration certificate is obtained. Non-resident shareholders may contribute in KRW or permitted foreign currency after completing the required foreign exchange declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA

THE UNDERSIGNED Director(s) and founding contributors of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, acting unanimously pursuant to the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Articles of Incorporation, do hereby resolve, ratify, and adopt the following actions effective immediately.

RESOLVED, that the Company confirms and ratifies the complete subscription of the registered contributed capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation. Each founding member has irrevocably subscribed to the capital assigned to them, and all contributions shall be fully paid in cash or lawful in-kind consideration before the filing of corporate registration. The paid-in capital shall be held in a blocked capital-verification account at a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea and shall remain unavailable for withdrawal until the corporate registration certificate is issued and the capital verification obligation is discharged.

RESOLVED, that the Company adopts the office address stated in the Articles of Incorporation as its sole registered office for legal service of process and official correspondence. The directors are expressly authorized to execute, amend, or terminate any lease, ownership consent, license, and third-party authorization necessary to secure and maintain the registered office and to notify the appropriate District Court Registry of such adoption.

RESOLVED, that the opening of one or more corporate bank accounts at licensed banks in the Republic of Korea is authorized. The banking mandate naming the representative director and any authorized officers is approved. Each authorized officer may open, operate, and close such accounts and shall sign jointly or individually within the limits established by the board.

RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed: one or more directors as provided in the Articles of Incorporation; one representative director who shall legally represent the Company within the scope of the Articles of Incorporation; and an auditor where required by law or by the Articles. Each officer shall serve until resignation, removal, or appointment of a successor. The officers are authorized to register their appointments with the District Court Registry and to complete all business registrations with the National Tax Service.

RESOLVED, that all acts performed by the officers and members prior to this resolution in furtherance of the Company’s formation are hereby ratified and confirmed as valid corporate actions.

RESOLVED, that this resolution shall be effective immediately and may be executed in multiple counterparts.

DATED this [date] at [city], Republic of Korea.

Signatures of the Director(s).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea - HomeTax e-Services portal at https://www.hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service - UNI-PASS portal at https://www.unipass.customs.go.kr for export declarations and clearance
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) obtains its TIN and VAT registration in one combined procedure. Within 20 days after commencement of business, file the statutory Business Registration Application with the competent District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered head office, using HomeTax or in-person submission through a certified tax accountant. The application must be accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, a power of attorney if filed by an agent, proof of the Korean business premises, identification of the domestic representative, and, where applicable, the foreign investment notification confirmation. After review, the District Tax Office issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN), which is simultaneously the VAT registration number and the corporate income tax reference number. A foreign non-resident entity with no Korean establishment that supplies electronic services to Korean end customers must appoint a domestic tax representative and file the statutory business registration application for foreign electronic service suppliers through HomeTax; NTS issues a foreign VAT identification number after validation. All VAT registrants must issue electronic tax invoices through HomeTax from the effective registration date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Korean domestic tax law; a Yuhan Hoesa is per se a Korean-resident corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold is applied to domestic business operators; VAT registration is mandatory upon business commencement. Simplified taxable status applies to businesses with annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000, but it is a reporting status rather than a registration exemption. Foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services with no Korean establishment must register under the NTS foreign-supplier registration path when supplying electronic services to Korean consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean VAT law mandates issuance of an electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) through HomeTax for B2B and export transactions. Registered suppliers transmit invoice data in real time to NTS via the HomeTax web service, NTS-certified API, or government-approved EDI, and each successful transmission receives an NTS reference number. The regime uses real-time filing and cross-matching with VAT returns rather than a pre-approval digital stamp; anti-fraud controls include automated abnormal-transaction detection and tax invoice audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Korean VAT Act for qualifying exports of enterprise SaaS when the service is supplied to a non-resident business customer, the service is actually used or consumed outside Korea, and the Korean exporter receives consideration from abroad in a convertible foreign currency. The exporter must retain the service contract, offshore delivery and usage evidence, and foreign exchange remittance documentation. For pure cloud-delivered SaaS, no physical customs movement is required, but the offshore service and foreign-currency collection evidence must be complete.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) accepted through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system for any physical goods exported
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing outward movement of physical media or hardware, if applicable
Commercial invoice and written service agreement with the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Foreign Exchange Settlement Record issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Service delivery and offshore usage records, such as cloud access logs, license agreement, or usage report, showing the SaaS is consumed outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to NTS export VAT review and tax invoice matching. If the customs, foreign-exchange, or offshore-usage evidence is missing, unverifiable, or false, NTS retroactively reclassifies the supply as taxable Korean supply, assesses VAT at 10% on the full invoice value, and imposes statutory additional tax of 20% for negligent under-declaration or 40% for fraudulent under-declaration, plus late-payment interest. Criminal penalties under the Korean tax crime punishment statutes can include imprisonment and fines, and the Framework Act on National Taxes permits retroactive reassessment for the fraudulent periods. Foreign-exchange repatriation violations may also draw penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the designated foreign exchange regulator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; daily administration delegated to designated foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized foreign exchange system anchored in the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions are freely convertible for cross-border payments of services, software license fees, royalties, and cost reimbursements, requiring only routine reporting through a designated foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment in the Korean LLC, are permitted under a positive-notification regime: an inward direct investment report must be filed with KOTRA or the designated bank before or within 30 days of remitting equity. Profit remittances, dividends, and liquidation proceeds are freely transferable after corporate tax settlement and documentary proof of the final beneficial owner's foreign residence, although the bank will require confirmation that no Korean tax arrears exist. KRW is subject to convertibility restrictions for non-resident bank accounts; non-residents cannot open won accounts solely for speculative trading, and our entity will need a permitted purpose such as payroll, vendor payments, or dividend reserve. The authorities may also verify that the SaaS transactions do not represent disguised cross-border lending or unlicensed money transmission. Overall, the regime is not a strict surrender currency system, but the entity must retain a professional transaction history and comply with the electronic reporting requirements under the Foreign Exchange Information Network to avoid lawful administrative penalties or currency clearance delays.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must be collected within 18 months from the export declaration date; there is no statutory percentage that must be converted into KRW. All proceeds must be credited to a designated foreign exchange account at a domestic bank and a certificate of export receipt must be lodged electronically with the bank. If collection exceeds 18 months, a notice of delay and prior approval schedule must be submitted to the Minister of Economy and Finance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Operating Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Deposit) and KRW Operating Account
Capital Escrow Account (FDI Capital Verification) and Trade Settlement Multi-Currency Account
Non-resident Direct Investment Receipt Account and USD/EUR Settlement Sub-Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Receipts Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: EMI cross-border viability is legally constrained. Because the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic resident entity, global fintech EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex or Stripe Treasury are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in Korea under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. They cannot offer a legally recognised KRW IBAN, won settlement relationship, or cross-border clearing access to the Korean interbank system without a licensed banking partner. A foreign EMI may act as an ancillary collection agent only if the payment is initiated outside Korea, but that does not apply to revenue collected from Korean enterprise customers. Therefore, fintech EMIs are rated Low as a treasury anchor; their permitted role is limited to supporting small-value overseas market expenses, and all critical liquidity must be held through the Tier-1 domestic commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Tier-1 banks require the statutory director, preferably the beneficial owner, to attend a physical in-branch KYC interview during initial onboarding. Fully remote opening is not statutorily mandated, and Financial Supervisory Service guidance emphasises in-person or equivalent identity verification; a notarised power of attorney or consular legalisation for non-resident shareholders is normally rejected for opening a new company's first operational account. For foreign investors, some high-tier banks allow an apostilled certification plus a recognised video call where the Korean substance is independently verified by a Korean certified public accountant and a local director is appointed. In practice, physical presence of at least one director remains the underwriting default for the KR_YUHANGHOESA entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director and non-resident final beneficial owner acting through a Korean registered LLC with limited local payroll
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation, certified shareholder register with beneficial ownership stages, passport copies with notarised translation, board resolution appointing the local/non-resident director, source-of-funds statement with supporting asset evidence, and a Korean CPA-prepared substance report covering registered office, monthly tax filing proof, payroll/mandatory insurance schedules and active SaaS platform operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: B2B SaaS revenue pattern shows high frequency of relatively small enterprise invoices inconsistent with typical cloud enterprise licensing and potential shell flow-through transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed enterprise subscription contracts with each material customer (seat count, term, service-level agreement and fee schedule), licensed IP and domain ownership certificates, transparent transaction ledger linked to bank references, customer legal entity KYC files, digital service export declaration forms where required, and a revenue recognition policy compliant with K-IFRS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection appears to be structured as third-party funding rather than authentic parent equity, risking disguised cross-border lending
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying investment agreement, audited previous financials of the foreign investor, group organisation chart, remitter bank statements, dedicated shareholder loan waiver and subordination letter, sworn affidavit confirming absence of repayment obligation or security surrogate, and a designated bank certificate of FDI report filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customer tail includes enterprises in jurisdictions subject to OFAC/EU/UN sanctions, increasing the odds of indirect sanctions exposure through cloud SaaS users
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated OFAC/EU/Korean LPO sanctions screening logs for all customers, denied-party list filtering settings, end-user identification policy, compliance attestation from the CEO, completed export control due diligence showing pure SaaS is outside dual-use physical goods and a mitigation plan with IP/device verification and red flag investigation workflow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the capital injection, the foreign shareholder must file an inward direct investment report with KOTRA or the designated bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before remitting equity. The funds must be wired through SWIFT MT103 with a clear narrative containing the receiver KR_YUHANGHOESA, the invoice/reference number, and the purpose code for foreign direct investment. After clearing in the bank's foreign investment deposit account, the bank issues a capital verification certificate confirming receipt and parity. For recurring SaaS revenue, each soft-funds remittance is routed via MT103 with the Foreign Exchange Information Network purpose code 223000 (computer and information services) or the code corresponding to the software license, and the bank will request the service contract, invoice and tax clearance record before crediting the operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the Korean entity should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for overseas cloud infrastructure, licensing royalties, reseller commissions and vendor payments, using the service-contract code in the Electronic Foreign Exchange Information System. For any hardware co-delivery to international enterprise clients, a commercial documentary letter of credit issued by the Tier-1 bank is the standard rail; documentary collections can be used for intercompany settlement within approved liquidity limits. The bank will maintain an open FX position register and require the entity to submit invoices, proof of exports (software delivery certificates) and compliance declarations to match the outbound payment against the declared business purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/KRW and EUR/KRW deliverable forward contracts approved for real current or capital transaction exposures, with maturity generally limited to 12 months
Onshore KRW/USD cross-currency swaps with identifiable hedge accounting linkage to the capital injection or recurring service invoices
Vanilla currency option packages (call/put) provided by Tier-1 banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act real-demand doctrine
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) and speculative KRW derivative positions are not permissible for non-financial domestic corporate treasury without prior regulatory approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Financial Statements Submission to DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end (December 31), i.e., no later than March 31; an extension of up to 20 days may be granted if the annual shareholders' general meeting is delayed by lawful circumstances and prior notice is filed with DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An administrative fine of up to KRW 50,000,000 (USD 37,000) for non-filing; listing of the company on DART non-compliance registry; daily fringe penalty tax of 0.03% of listed company revenue for continuous default only if externally listed; repeated non-filing triggers mandatory inspection by the FSS and referral for criminal penalty under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Franchise Tax Declaration and Payment (Di Fa Se)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government Tax Office (Si/Gun/Gu) within the address of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed annual window: March 1 through March 31 of each year for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty equal to 3% of the unpaid tax if paid after the deadline; if still unpaid after 30 days, a monthly delinquency interest of 0.66% applies; sustained non-payment for 6 months may lead to compulsory collection, business activity freeze, and administrative strike-off of the corporate license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Business License Annual Renewal (Business Registration Certificate Validation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Tax Office under the National Tax Service or designated local administrative e-government portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual validation is performed by the tax authority before the renewal of the electronic tax invoice certification; the business owner must confirm and update business registration details by February 10 for the start of the commercial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inactive or suspended business registration triggers immediate loss of electronic tax invoice issuance rights; VAT input tax credit is disallowed; the company is subjected to zero-return declarations and possible forced closure through local administrative measures if registration remains lapsed for 3 consecutive months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission to the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the electronic tax filing system (HomeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual general shareholders' meeting, which itself must be held by March 31 for a fiscal year ending December 31; therefore, the submission is no later than May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the required audited financial statements leads to a tax surcharge of 0.5% of the subject sales, plus administrative fines up to KRW 20,000,000; the NTS may issue an audit order that designates a third-party CPA at the company's expense; persistent failure is treated as bad faith filing and could trigger a comprehensive tax investigation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit is compulsory under the Korean External Audit Law and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if any one of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (1) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million); (2) annual revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million); (3) the entity has 300 or more full-time employees during the fiscal year; (4) the entity is classified as a large corporation under the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act with total assets above KRW 500 billion; (5) the entity has parent-subsidiary relations with a company that is already subject to external audit; (6) total outstanding borrowings and liabilities to financial institutions exceed KRW 12 billion; or (7) the entity is a public concern designated by the Financial Services Commission for investor protection. For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa operating a B2B Enterprise SaaS business, even if none of these thresholds is met, the Ministry of Government Legislation requires an audit if shareholders holding at least 5% of the equity demand one. For SME exemption, entities with assets below KRW 12 billion must follow simplified accounting standards and do not require certified audit unless they meet the revenue or headcount triggers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board (K-IFRS) for entities that are legally required to undergo external audit and are listed or 'designated corporations'; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for entities whose securities are not publicly traded and did not meet the large corporation definition; SME accounting standards under the K-IFRS 'General Standard for Small and Medium Enterprises' available for entities with assets under KRW 12 billion, revenue under KRW 10 billion, and headcount below 300; all standards mandate accrual basis, faithful representation, and compliance with the Framework of Korean Accounting Standards, and all audited statements must be attached to the annual tax return

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an accurate Register of Members and must file any ownership transfer, share pledge, or beneficial ownership change with the Korean Registry Office within 30 days of the transaction date. Annually, within 90 days after the fiscal year end (no later than March 31), the company must file an Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation Statement through the Court Registration Information Center or the corporate registry. This statement must list each beneficial owner who holds or controls more than 4% of equity interest or voting rights, but 1% is the reporting threshold for foreign-owned SMEs under the Act on Foreign Investment Promotion. If any shareholding change occurs during the year, a mandatory disclosure notice must be reported to the NTS within 30 days of the change for foreign shareholders. Failure to meet the 30-day reporting window results in administrative fines of KRW 1,000,000 to KRW 10,000,000 per violation, and the unregistered share transfer is invalid against third parties under the Korean Commercial Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 to USD 4,000 per annum depending on Seoul central business district versus regional location, inclusion of registered agent services, and legal correspondence handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 to USD 30,000 for a certified independent audit of a B2B enterprise SaaS company with moderate cross-border revenue, prepared and audited under K-IFRS or K-GAAP by a licensed Korean CPA firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% maximum combined rate (22% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge; progressive lower rates apply below KRW 20 billion taxable income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea offers statutory tax holidays for new growth-engine and innovative businesses, Free Economic Zone (FEZ) incentives including 3-year full and 2-year 50% corporate tax reduction, R&D deduction/credit up to 30-50% of qualifying R&D costs, job-creation tax credits, profit repatriation tax deferrals for foreign-invested companies in special zones, and reduced rates for small and medium enterprises under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, filed via the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a standard December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate identity and foreign ownership disclosure: company name, corporate registration number, business registration number, tax office, industry code (ISIC 6201), and details of non-resident shareholders including name, address, foreign TIN, shareholding percentage and country of tax residence
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Furnish the complete chain of foreign shareholders with exact foreign TINs and registered addresses. A Yuhan Hoesa LLC with non-resident ownership must attach the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation and tax residency certificate. Failure to complete this box accurately may trigger treaty benefit denial and additional withholding assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements annex: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, and statement of changes in equity prepared under K-IFRS or Korean GAAP, showing all operating revenue from B2B cloud SaaS subscriptions, software licenses, implementation fees, and any foreign-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate Korean-source subscription revenues from foreign-source revenues. For non-resident customers, apply the Korean deemed-source rules under Article 119 of the Income Tax Act and Article 93 of the Corporate Tax Act. Cross-border cloud software services physically performed through servers in Korea may be treated as Korean-source income and therefore must be fully disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: add non-deductible expenses, reserve additions, non-taxable revenue, and adjustments for tax depreciation, entertainment expenses, and intercompany pricing corrections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned subsidiaries must adjust for any transfer pricing upward or downward adjustments in accordance with the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Disallow excessive management fees, royalties, and interest paid to foreign related parties that fail the arm's length standard. Declare any foreign tax credits originating from related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation and loss carryforward application: compute total tax base after applying non-deductible expense additions, deductible reserve reversals, carried-forward net operating losses, and intra-group loss relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Clearly list the Korean-source taxable income attributable to the SaaS business. For loss carryforwards, the maximum carryforward period is 10 years for most corporations. Non-resident entities with permanent establishments must attach a schedule allocating overhead and central administration costs to the Korean PE. Avoid double counting foreign taxes in the local taxable income calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base and rate schedule: apply the progressive national corporate income tax rates (10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 22% above KRW 20 billion), then add the 10% local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean limited liability company owned by non-residents, the entity is treated as a separate taxpayer and profits are taxed at the entity level. Do not consolidate foreign parent losses into the Korean entity. Compute the local income tax surcharge on the national corporate income tax and report separately in the ancillary tax schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and deduction incentives: compute R&D credits, job-creation credits, foreign tax credit, tax credits for investment facilities, and deductions for Free Economic Zone or special R&D zones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean SaaS operation claims R&D credits for cloud software development, maintain contemporaneous project budgets, payroll details, and patent/output documents. Non-resident shareholders may also claim a unilateral foreign tax credit for Korean withholding taxes when those income items are reported in their home jurisdiction. Attach supporting certificates from authorized tax accountants.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing adjustments and related-party transaction schedule: disclose all transactions with overseas affiliated companies, including intercompany SaaS license fees, royalty payments, management charges, cloud infrastructure payments, loans, and any intangible property sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every non-resident-owned Korean entity must complete this box comprehensively. If the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction value exceeds KRW 10 billion, attach the Master File and Local File contemporaneously. State the selected transfer pricing methodology (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split) and justify the arm's length comparability analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Outbound dividend, interest, and royalty withholding tax declaration: report any dividends declared to foreign shareholders, interest paid to foreign lenders, and royalties paid to foreign licensors; calculate the aggregate 22% domestic withholding rate (20% national plus 2% local surcharge) or the reduced treaty rate if applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean entity acts as withholding agent. Attach the Foreign Tax Residency Certificate (issued by the foreign competent authority), a Beneficial Ownership Statement, and proof of qualification for the treaty rate. Without this documentation, the full 22% withholding tax must be paid and remitted to the NTS within the statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and DTA relief reconciliation: report income source jurisdiction, tax paid abroad, treaty article, and credit limitation calculation under the foreign tax credit system
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parents claiming DTA relief must ensure the entitlement threshold is satisfied: the recipient must be the beneficial owner, have tax residency in the treaty state, and maintain substantive economic substance. Where treaty rates require a minimum shareholding period (e.g., 10% participation for 12 months for reduced dividend rates), attach the Korean resident shareholder register and transactional records proving the holding period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax computation and payments: aggregate annual tax amount, subtract prepayments and prior payments, compute final balance due, and declare whether intercompany transactions have been documented as part of the OECD-compliant filing package
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For outbound profit repatriation, ensure all withholding tax obligations are settled in the same annual period as the distribution. The Korean entity's failure to report hidden distributions will expose both the entity and directors to additional tax, penalties, and possible criminal referral. Confirm the final filing uses official NTS paper forms plus the electronic data transmission package.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers additional tax under Framework Act on Taxes Article 47-3: 20% of the unpaid tax for ordinary corporations (10% for small and medium enterprises), with an additional daily unpaid-tax penalty of 0.025% per day from the due date. Negligent under-reporting generally attracts 20% of the omitted amount, rising to 40% for insufficient disclosure and 60% for fraudulent concealment. Criminal referral occurs for willful tax evasion, with imprisonment up to five years or a fine not exceeding five times the evaded tax amount under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory dividend withholding rate (20% national withholding tax and 2% local income tax surcharge) on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders, subject to reduction under an applicable Double Tax Treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty withholding, the non-resident shareholder must, before payment, furnish the Korean withholding agent with: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction, endorsed under the Korea treaty; (ii) a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming the shareholder is the actual owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty income and has no contractual or legal obligation to pass it to another person; (iii) supporting evidence of owning the requisite shareholding percentage (often 10% or more) for the required continuous period (typically 12 months) as required for reduced dividend rates; and (iv) a completed Application for Tax Treaty Tax Rate Reduction or Exemption using the NTS prescribed form filed through HomeTax. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident can file a refund claim with the NTS within five years by submitting the full documentation package and evidence that the normal withholding was excessive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Cross-border royalties of any kind are subject to a 22% aggregate statutory withholding tax (20% national plus 2% local surcharge); most Korea tax treaties reduce royalties to 10%-15%. Interest payments to foreign lenders carry the same 22% aggregate statutory rate, with treaty rates commonly 10%-15% (some treaties provide lower or zero interest withholding). The lower treaty rate requires the same TRC and beneficial ownership proof, plus for royalties the recipient must not be the economic owner of the trademark, copyright, or software if the transaction is structured as a stripped royalty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) of aggregate cross-border transactions with foreign related parties in a fiscal year triggers mandatory contemporaneous Master File and Local File preparation; multi-national groups with consolidated annual revenue above KRW 100 billion are also required to file a Country-by-Country Report (CbCR).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a broad substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on Taxes, the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and the general anti-abuse rule. Although Korea does not apply formal UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, the NTS will disregard or re-characterize transactions that lack commercial substance and valuable economic effect. A foreign-owned Korean SaaS entity must maintain real board meetings, substantive employment, office premises, servers or infrastructure in Korea, and genuine risk-management functions in Korea. For treaty relief and transfer pricing defense, the overseas related party must satisfy a CIGA-like test by having actual employees, premises, and decision-making authority over the relevant intangible asset and investment functions; a shell company without real activity will be denied treaty benefits and may trigger penalty assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting B2B SaaS subscription revenue, fabricating service invoices from online payment processors, or concealing related-party royalty income by booking software license income in a no-tax jurisdiction while continuing to receive payments into Korean bank accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Articles 3 and 9: imprisonment for up to five years and a fine not exceeding five times the evaded corporate income tax; additionally under Framework Act on Taxes Article 47-3, fraudulent concealment attracts a 60% additional tax penalty on the underreported amount, plus daily interest and corrective assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under Korean Commercial Act Article 401(2): directors who intentionally or grossly negligently perform their duties and cause harm to the tax authority or third parties are jointly and severally liable to compensate the state for unpaid taxes, penalties, and costs. NTS may impose travel bans (blacklisting) and issue compulsory investigation referrals for criminal contempt; the responsible director can be arrested and imprisoned for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an outward shell company in Hong Kong, Singapore, or a zero-tax state without employees, business premises, or storage ability, solely to hold shares in the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and collect dividends, interest, or royalties while claiming reduced treaty withholding rates under the Korea-Hong Kong, Korea-Singapore or other double tax conventions when the real beneficial owner is not resident there
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 6(2) and the general anti-abuse rule, the NTS may deny the DTA benefit and re-impose the full 22% withholding tax on the entire distribution, plus interest charges; the Framework Act on Taxes Articles 15 and 42 support re-characterizing the shell as transparent or invalid, effectively making the Korean entity liable for the shortfall and civil fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or directed the treaty-abusive shell structure are jointly and severally liable for the shortfall in withholding tax and penalties under Commercial Act Article 401(2). NTS will blacklist the directors, impose travel restrictions, and may prosecute them for aiding tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to five years and personal monetary restitution of all mispaid treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's length intercompany licensing agreements with an affiliated foreign SaaS group whereby the Korean entity pays excessive royalties, management fees, or interest for marketing intangibles or software source code that is not substantively connected to the Korean business, thereby reducing the Korean taxable base far below the OECD arm's length result and failing to prepare or submit a Local File/Master File at the KRW 10 billion threshold
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 4 requires the NTS to re-determine the arm's length price and adjust the Korean taxable income accordingly; the additional tax will bear an unfaithful-return penalty of 40%-60% under Framework Act on Taxes Article 47-2 and 47-3, plus interest and daily unpaid-tax surcharges. Massive transfer pricing adjustments may also trigger referral to the Tax Tribunal and criminal investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorized non-arm's length pricing are personally liable under Korean Commercial Act Article 401(2) for the resulting unpaid corporate tax and penalty amounts; the NTS can attach directors' personal assets and impose a travel ban (blacklisting) pending compliance. In cases of willful falsification of transfer pricing documentation, the director faces criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to five times the manipulated tax amount.
